subject: Ampersand POC kickstart — logistics, load test window, onsite vs virtual
messages:
From: Amy Park <amy@ampersand.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Ampersand POC kickstart: scheduling & access

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for moving quickly here — wed like to get the POC kickstart on the calendar for the week of Mar 22. High level ask: a half-day hands-on session (prompt review, routing walkthrough, and a light load validation) plus a follow-up deep-dive for integration/ops.

Questions from our side so we can firm up logistics:
- Do you run the load validation onsite or can we do it remotely? Were expecting ~20–30 concurrent user sessions for peak scenario.
- For onsite: what are typical AV/room requirements and how long should we reserve the lab?
- For virtual: do you require special network/firewall configuration to allow sustained concurrent connections?
- Can Redwood record the session? Well need recording permission for our internal team.
- Please share a proposed agenda and any checklist (security, visitor badge process, NDAs) we should follow.

Attaching a short note with our preferred windows. Our security lead is copied: ops@ampersand.ai.

Best,
Amy Park
Head of Engineering, Ampersand Retail
Amy Park | amy@ampersand.ai

Attachments: ampersand_windows.pdf (1 page)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Amy Park <amy@ampersand.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-10T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ampersand POC kickstart: scheduling & access

Hi Amy — thanks, and great to meet you (virtually). Happy to run a hybrid flow that covers both hands-on prompt work and a separate system/deployment deep-dive. Quick responses to your bullets and a proposed plan below.

Answers / proposal:
- Load validation: we can do either. For lower-risk accounts we often run initial throughput/load tests from our Dedicated staging pool remotely (no need for onsite hardware). If you want to validate your on-prem network path or AV routing we can instead do an onsite mini-load with our engineers present.
- Room/AV: For an onsite half-day we typically request: projector or large monitor, wired gigabit Ethernet to the room (for consistent throughput), one breakout table for the prompt lab (6 seats) and ability to present from two machines. Plan 3.5–4 hours to include setup and a 60-minute load window.
- Virtual config: open outbound TCP to our endpoint (443) and allow longer idle timeouts for stable streams. We'll send a minimal firewall checklist.
- Recording: Redwood can record; please confirm in writing. We keep recordings on our secure storage and can share a link.
- Agenda & checklist: attaching agenda_v1.pdf and a short onboarding checklist.

Proposed calendar:
- Option A (onsite): Tue Mar 22, 0900–1330 PT — onsite half-day (setup 0900–0930, prompts & routing 0930–1130, load & validation 1130–1230, buffer 1230–1330)
- Option B (virtual): Wed Mar 23, 0900–1200 PT — virtual hands-on + routing, evening 2000–2100 PT load window (off-hours) if you prefer less impact to your day-to-day systems.

Marissa (SE) is looped in — shell own the prompt workshop and load plan. A couple of asks for you to confirm:
- final attendee list and their roles (well tailor the prompt review accordingly)
- expected concurrent sessions for the load window
- confirmation on recording permission

Thanks — Ill hold the times tentatively once you confirm which option you prefer.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124

Attachments: agenda_v1.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Amy Park <amy@ampersand.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-11T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ampersand POC kickstart: scheduling & access

Thanks Amy / Soojin — looping in the technical plan so you have the details for the hands-on portion.

Planned runbook for the half-day (if onsite):
- 0930–1000: initial prompt walkthrough (prompt templates, guardrails, expected outputs)
- 1000–1100: routing & model-choice workshop (showing fallback to smaller quantized variants and cost/latency tradeoffs)
- 1100–1130: break & quick environment checks
- 1130–1230: 60-minute controlled load window (we simulate traffic from our staging pool and, if youd like, from a box in your network).
- 1230–1300: result review and next steps (metrics, token cost estimates, recommended quantization)

For the load window we need the following from Ampersand:
- IP allowlist for the machine(s) you want us to hit (if remotely testing your infra) or a wired Ethernet port in the room if onsite.
- A single test dataset or a short list of prompt examples representing peak stitching/throughput. If you prefer, Marissa can generate synthetic traces that match expected QPS.
- A host contact on the day for on-site badge and AV troubleshooting.

I've attached the onboarding_checklist.xlsx that covers badge process, parking, and network details. For recording: we prefer to record the prompt walkthrough and load graphs; if there are embargoed artifacts please flag them now.

Also note: if we do an onsite run, please ensure a quiet room with stable power — last-minute interruptions can skew load numbers. If you want, we can run a small pre-check one business day before (15–20 min).

— Marissa Cole
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: onboarding_checklist.xlsx
From: Amy Park <amy@ampersand.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@ampersand.ai
Date: 2027-03-12T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ampersand POC kickstart: scheduling & access

Hi Soojin / Marissa — thanks for the clear plan. Well take Option A onsite for an in-person kickoff on Tue Mar 22, 0900–1330 PT. A few confirmations:

- Attendees: Amy Park (Head Eng), Ravi Khanna (Infra lead), Elena Soto (Platform), +8 product engineers — total 11 in-room; plus 4 remote observers.
- Load expectations: please design for 25 concurrent sessions as our target peak. Well provide a small sample prompt set (3 templates) by Monday 3/21.
- Recording: confirmed — you may record the sessions. Well mark any sensitive segments before hand if needed.
- Visitor access: our building requires visitor badges. Onsite host is Ravi Khanna (ravi.k@ampersand.ai). Ravi will add Soojin and Marissa to the guest list and provide a parking pass.
- AV: large display + 1 wired Ethernet port is available in Room B23.

We appreciate the pre-check offer — please do a 20-minute connectivity check on Mon 3/21 at 1600 PT.

See you in person — well send the attendee list and the prompt set early next week.

Best,
Amy
